subject: EngageX discovery: infra/auth/routing + observability playbook
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@engagex.ai>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@engagex.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: EngageX discovery: infra/auth/routing + observability playbook

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the EngageX infra and ML teams. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive next week.

Key notes from today's discovery:
- Primary use case: real-time QA assistant in their customer support console (sub-400ms target for 95th pct when cached; 800ms cold).
- Routing: want per-tenant cost tier routing (prod vs sandbox) and fallback on lower-capacity model when Dedicated pool is saturated.
- Auth: prefer short-lived service account tokens (OIDC) from their IdP for server-to-server calls; customer data must never be used for Redwood model training.
- Outputs: They need structured JSON responses (tool-calling + structured output schema) and candidate reranking for top-K retrieval.
- Observability: require trace-id propagation from front-end to Redwood, and breakdown headers (queue/batch/compute) surfaced in logs and dashboards.

Immediate next steps (owner):
1) Redwood to share a short "integration playbook" doc that includes sample SDK auth flow (service account + OIDC), an example route policy for model fallback, and a minimal observability contract (trace header names, latency breakdown keys). (Sean, by Mon 8/24)
2) EngageX to share a diagram of their request path and any existing trace header names. (Sophie, by Fri 8/28)
3) Schedule 60m technical deep-dive to walk SDK snippet, embeddings->reranker plan, and dashboard wireframe. (Tom & Camila to agree on slots)

Attachments: I uploaded a first-pass playbook and a tiny SDK snippet for Node (redwood-sample-sdk-snippet.txt) — see attached.

If anything is missing or mis-captured, please reply inline. Otherwise propose 8/26 or 8/27 for the deep-dive.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

From: Sophie Park <sophie@engagex.ai>

Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EngageX discovery: infra/auth/routing + observability playbook

Thanks Sean — helpful summary. Couple clarifying questions before the deep-dive: 

1) Auth: Our infra team prefers using our IdP (Okta) to mint short-lived OIDC tokens for backend services. Does Redwood support exchanging an OIDC token for a per-request service token, or do we need to manage a static API key per service? We'd prefer not to store long-lived keys.

2) Embeddings + reranker: we plan to index support docs and surface top-10 candidates, then run a reranker for final top-3. Does Redwood recommend running the reranker as a separate model call, or use structured output + rerank inside a single request? Any latency guidance for each approach?

3) Observability: we use a tracing header X-Trace-Id in our stack. Can you confirm the exact header names Redwood will accept and whether Redwood will return a latency-breakdown header we can capture at our gateway?

Proposed deep-dive: 8/26 11:00am PT — does that work?

Attaching our infra diagram for reference (engagex-infra-diagram.png).

Sophie Park
Head of Platform Engineering, EngageX
sophie@engagex.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: EngageX discovery: infra/auth/routing + observability playbook

Sean / Camila — a few technical clarifications I prepared to bring to the deep-dive. Please use these as the baseline in the playbook: 

Auth flow (recommended):
- Support OIDC service-to-service: EngageX tokens from Okta can be exchanged via Redwood's token-exchange endpoint for short-lived per-request JWTs (ttl ~5m). No static API keys required. We'll include example curl + Node code in the playbook.

Routing & fallbacks:
- Suggest policy: route("prod") -> Dedicated pool (pinned model v1.2) with fallback to hosted quantized variant (v1.2-q4) if queue depth > threshold. We'll include an example policy block for their router config.

Embeddings & rerank pattern:
- Recommended: run retrieval (embedding similarity) to get top-10 locally, then issue a dedicated reranker call to a smaller T5-style model for final top-3. This separates concerns and keeps reranker compute smaller (lower p95 cost). Expect ~30–120ms extra for reranker depending on model size; we'll add measured examples.

Observability contract (minimal):
- Accept inbound header X-Trace-Id or traceparent (W3C). Redwood will echo the same header in responses and also inject a Redwood-Trace header with a unique internal id.
- Latency breakdown header: X-Redwood-Latency: queue=12;batch=8;compute=180;total=200 (ms). We'll document exact keys and provide sample JSON logs and a Grafana dashboard wireframe.

I'll patch the sample SDK snippet with the token-exchange flow and a tiny function showing how to pass X-Trace-Id through the request. Attaching the snippet now.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Integration Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: EngageX discovery: infra/auth/routing + observability playbook

Appreciate the clarity Neha. A few follow-ups before the call: 

- The latency-breakdown header is perfect — we plan to record those at the API gateway and surface per-call in our request logs. Can you confirm whether the X-Redwood-Latency header is emitted for both cached and cold requests?

- For trace correlation, we currently propagate X-Trace-Id and would like Redwood to accept that and also include the Redwood-Trace in your logs so we can map events cross-system.

- Can you add a small example of structured output schema for the assistant actions (tool call invocation + arguments) so our front-end can render buttons and suggested actions? A JSON schema example would be ideal.

8/26 11:00am PT works for us — sending calendar invite.

Tom Wu
